sections.h2: Bountiful's layout and what it means for a house
sections.html:
Bountiful sits in Davis County on the slope between the Wasatch Range and the Great Salt Lake flats, at about 4,771 feet and roughly 13 square miles. The 2020 count was 45,762 people in 15,427 households and 15,945 housing units. Few lots are left to build on, so most sales are resales of houses with decades of wear.

Old downtown is at the foot of the mountains, homes climb the eastern benches, and the west side is flat and runs toward the lake. Most land east of the city is Forest Service ground, which is why the hillside streets stop where public land starts. North Salt Lake, Woods Cross, West Bountiful and Centerville are the neighbors. A bench-street lot and a west-side lot are very different properties, and buyers know it.

A typical year brings about 23 inches of precipitation and about 59 inches of snow, with a record high of 104 degrees and a record low of minus 9. Roofs, furnaces and cooling systems all get used. Inspectors in a snow climate usually look first at the roof surface, attic insulation and gutters, so expect questions if those have not been touched in years.

The Wasatch Fault follows the base of the range, and more than 85 percent of Utahns live in the earthquake zone along the Wasatch Front. Unreinforced masonry is a particular worry. If your Bountiful house is older brick, a buyer may ask about chimneys, foundations and any retrofit.

  • Roof age and snow load on the east benches
  • Brick chimneys and masonry walls
  • Drainage on steep hillside lots
  • Furnace and water heater age

Interstate 15 is the main road, and FrontRunner commuter rail has served the city since April 2008. Legacy Parkway opened on September 13, 2008, to ease pressure on the interstate. The narrow gap into Salt Lake County still slows rush hour, which is worth a line for buyers who commute south. Houses a short drive from the Mueller Park Canyon trailheads tend to draw extra attention from hikers.

sections.h2: Closing out electric and water service
sections.html:
Bountiful City runs its own electric department and also handles utility billing. The power office is at 198 South 200 West. Utility billing is 801-298-6100, and the 24-hour outage line is 801-298-6072. City Hall is at 795 South Main Street.

A live utility representative has to set up or end service, which rules out an online form. Call ahead of closing. With the sale date fixed, the last meter reading and final bill are easier to settle.

  • Call 801-298-6100 to schedule the end of service.
  • Ask for a final meter reading on the closing date.
  • Say where the final bill should be mailed.
  • Keep a copy of the closed account.

sections.h2: How Bountiful property tax is billed and paid
sections.html:
Davis County bills Bountiful property tax, and payment is due each year on November 30. When November 30 falls on a weekend, the deadline rolls to the next business day. Pay at the treasurer's office, 61 South Main Street, Room 105, Farmington, or call 801-451-3243.

Utah Code 59-2-103 cuts residential value by 45 percent, so 55 percent is taxed. Land counts toward that cut only up to one acre for each residential unit.

Davis County payment schedule
Payment itemDate or amount
Payment dueNovember 30
Late penaltyGreater of $10 or 2.5 percent per parcel
Reduced penalty if paid by January 31Greater of $10 or 1 percent
Interest after January 317.25 to 10 percent
Where to pay in person61 S. Main St., Room 105, Farmington

If a lender escrows your taxes, it may pay through a third-party service, and that can delay posting by several days. Check the account before you list.

Your Notice of Property Market Valuation carries the appeal deadline. Submit the Board of Equalization form to the Davis County Controller, one application for each parcel, giving your own view of value as of January 1. Questions go to 801-451-3323.

Acceptable proof includes a recent closing statement, a full appraisal, three or more comparable sales within one mile, an income statement, a documented factual error, or evidence of damage. The appeal covers this year's market value only. The tax rate cannot be challenged.

Selling mid-year does not end an appeal, because both it and the bill follow the property. Let the buyer's side know what is pending so any refund is routed properly.

Selling for cash avoids the lender appraisal and repair haggling that tend to follow a listing, and the date is yours to pick. Four steps cover it.

  1. Describe the house honestly, tenants, liens and repairs included.
  2. Take the buyer's offer or turn it down.
  3. Escrow opens, title is searched and payoffs are requested.
  4. You sign, escrow divides the year's tax between you and the buyer, and the money is yours.

Bring the latest tax notice and any loan payoff details. If a tenant lives there, bring the lease so move-out terms can be written into the contract.

Before the title company opens escrow, pull together the newest Davis County tax notice, proof that any lender-escrowed tax was posted, the mortgage payoff figure and the age of the roof, furnace and water heater. Older Bountiful houses draw questions on all three systems, and a written answer beats a guess. Add the valuation notice if an appeal is pending, and the lease if the house is rented.

Sellers of inherited houses should also gather whatever shows who may sign. The title company will want every signature collected before it sets a date, and that step usually decides how long the sale takes.

sections.h2: What Bountiful sellers usually run into
sections.html:
People who sell fast in Bountiful tend to own an older house, a hillside lot, or a place they must move quickly.

  • Older homes that need roof, electrical or plumbing work before a retail buyer can get a loan
  • Inherited houses where several relatives must agree before anyone signs
  • Rentals with tenants in place and a lease that runs past the sale date
  • Overdue repairs that make a traditional listing hard to price

If you are unsure which bucket your house falls in, a quick walk-through with a contractor or inspector gives you a written list of what a retail buyer would ask you to fix. Compare that list against the offer you would get as-is before you spend money on repairs.

The resale pool is wide because the city is close to Salt Lake City and on the FrontRunner line. That helps a well-kept house. It does less for a property that needs work, which is where an as-is sale fits.

faqs.q: What county is Bountiful in, and who bills the property tax?
faqs.a: Davis County bills it. Its treasurer collects at 61 South Main Street in Farmington, phone 801-451-3243.

faqs.q: When is Bountiful property tax due?
faqs.a: November 30, or the next business day if that is a weekend. Paying late costs the greater of $10 or 2.5 percent per parcel.

faqs.q: Is there a way to lower the taxable value on a Bountiful house?
faqs.a: Your primary residence already gets the 45 percent reduction. If the market value on your notice seems too high, appeal to the Board of Equalization through the Davis County Controller before the printed date.

faqs.q: Who do I call to stop electric service when I sell?
faqs.a: Bountiful City utility billing at 801-298-6100. A representative must handle the request, so schedule it before closing.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Bountiful house that has tenants or needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. A house with tenants, put-off repairs or an inherited title can sell as it stands. Be open about lease terms and condition so the date and move-out terms are agreed early.
